name: NAV Lending and Fund Finance
summary: Fund-level leverage from either side: lending to a fund (NAV facility, subscription line, hybrid) or to a GP, or being an LP in a fund that borrows. Subscription lines raise reported IRR with no change in multiple; NAV facilities fund bolt-ons, rescues (often PIK) or distributions, and NAV-funded distributions inflate IRR and DPI and are often recallable. The spine is: LPA authority and LPAC consent; LTV on independent marks with stress at 25% to 40% haircuts and crisis advance rates; cash sweep and cure waterfall; cross-collateralization and structural subordination; full leverage-stack map; amendment history; and DPI and IRR without the sub line and without NAV-funded distributions. All of it is contractual since June 2024. GP financing (loans to GPs against fees and carry) is not covered in the bible; items for it are derived by analogy and flagged in refs.
one_check: Ask for DPI and IRR without the subscription line and without NAV-loan-funded distributions; if the GP cannot or will not produce them, you do not know the fund's real liquidity or return.

subtypes.name: NAV loan
subtypes.description: Loan against the fund's portfolio (pledge of holding-company equity), typically after the investment period.

subtypes.name: Subscription line
subtypes.description: Loan against LPs' uncalled commitments; bridges capital calls.

subtypes.name: Hybrid facility
subtypes.description: Blends NAV collateral and recourse to uncalled commitments.

subtypes.name: GP financing
subtypes.description: Loan to the GP or management company against fees, carry or GP commitments (not covered in the bible; derived items).

intake_questions.question: Is this a NAV loan, subscription line, hybrid facility, or GP-level financing?
Are we the lender, or an LP in the borrowing fund?
intake_questions.why: Determines whether lender protections or LP protections lead.

intake_questions.question: What is the use of proceeds: bolt-ons, rescue of portfolio companies, or distributions?
intake_questions.why: Distribution use triggers recall and carry tests.

intake_questions.question: Is the GP raising, or about to raise, a successor fund?
Is the facility rated, and by whom?
What other facilities exist in the fund's leverage stack?

requests.request: Facility agreement (or draft) and fee letter.
requests.format: Execution or latest draft, with all schedules and the fee letter.
requests.why: All-in cost and the terms that govern sweeps, cures and recourse live here.
requests.pass: Complete agreement and fee letter received.
requests.fail: Fee letter withheld or schedules missing.
requests.verify: Compare with the version the administrator holds.

requests.request: Use-of-proceeds statement: offensive (bolt-ons, refinancing), defensive (rescue of portfolio companies) or liquidity (distributions), with amounts by use.
requests.format: Signed statement by the GP with a schedule by portfolio company or distribution.
requests.why: About 80% of NAV facilities supported portfolio companies and about 20% funded distributions; distributions inflate DPI and may be recallable.
requests.pass: Use of proceeds stated by amount; any distribution use disclosed to LPs with recall terms.
requests.fail: Use is 'distributions' in a fund raising its next vintage, or uses not itemized.
requests.verify: Trace proceeds through the fund's bank account after drawdown.

requests.request: LPA clause permitting fund-level borrowing, and the LPAC consent record for this facility.
requests.format: LPA extract and signed LPAC consent.
requests.why: ILPA says GPs should seek LPAC consent regardless of use of proceeds.
requests.pass: LPA permits the facility type and amount; LPAC consented in writing before signing.
requests.fail: No borrowing authority, or no LPAC consent.
requests.verify: Confirm consent with an LPAC member.

requests.request: Borrowing-base and LTV definitions, eligible-asset criteria and concentration limits.
requests.why: Definitions determine when LTV breaches and what counts as collateral.
requests.pass: Definitions objective; ineligible and concentrated assets excluded or haircut.

requests.request: Portfolio schedule: every asset with NAV, cost, sector, leverage and date of last mark; top-3 assets as % of NAV; number of assets.
requests.why: Concentration magnifies a single-asset failure.
requests.pass: Top-3 share and asset count within facility limits.
requests.fail: Top-3 assets dominate NAV or few assets.
requests.verify: Tie to the fund's latest quarterly report and audit.

requests.request: Map of the full fund-level leverage stack (subscription line, NAV facility, asset-based facilities) with each facility's margin-call and default triggers.
requests.format: Single diagram plus a table of facilities, balances, maturities and triggers.
requests.why: Multiple layers with no single map hide how a shock propagates.
requests.pass: Single complete map; triggers do not cascade.

requests.request: Fundraising status: whether the GP is raising, or will raise within 24 months, a successor fund.
requests.why: Interim IRR and DPI inflation near a fundraise is a named concern.
requests.pass: No fundraise within the facility's distribution window, or no distribution use.
requests.fail: Distribution use timed to a fundraise.

requests.request: Subscription-line profile: size as % of commitments, history of days outstanding, LP opt-out offered, uncalled-capital estimate.
requests.why: Sub lines raise IRR without changing multiple.
requests.pass: <= 15% to 25% of commitments and <= 180 days outstanding (ILPA PE reference points); opt-out offered.
requests.fail: Above 25% or beyond 180 days without disclosure; no opt-out.

requests.request: Rating-agency report if the facility or a feeder note is rated.
requests.why: Agencies stress fund value 40% to 60% and may rate to the most conservative permitted terms.
requests.pass: Rating report reviewed; stress assumptions understood.

requests.request: GP-level financing package: management-company and GP financial statements, projected management fees and carry, and the interests to be pledged.
requests.format: Audited or reviewed financials; projection model.
requests.why: GP financing is not covered in the bible; by analogy, fixed fees dominate GP revenue and carry is uncertain.
requests.pass: Debt service covered by contracted management fees alone.
requests.verify: Tie fee projections to LPAs and fund sizes.

requests.request: Initial and maximum LTV, with the NAV on which LTV is tested (GP marks or independent valuation).
requests.why: LTV on GP marks hides breaches.
requests.pass: Initial LTV about 10% to 30%, maximum around 40% as downside buffer (Sidley, Aug. 2025); tested on independent or lender-approved valuations.
requests.fail: Initial LTV above 30% or tested on GP marks only.

requests.request: Cash-sweep and LTV step-down mechanics, cure rights and the cure waterfall.
requests.why: Cash sweeps are critical to refinancing risk; no sweep is a red flag.
requests.pass: Mandatory sweep that steps up as LTV rises; cure rights limited and time-bound.
requests.fail: No cash sweep; unlimited equity cures.

requests.request: Lender right to commission third-party valuations of collateral.
requests.why: Stale marks hide LTV breaches; lenders should retain rights to third-party valuations.
requests.pass: Lender may commission independent valuations at least annually and on events.

requests.request: Testing schedule: initial, periodic and event-driven LTV tests.
requests.why: Testing only at fixed dates misses intra-period shocks.
requests.pass: Initial, periodic (at least quarterly) and event-driven tests.

requests.request: Schedule of pledged assets and cross-collateralization terms, including whether one asset's default triggers the whole facility.
requests.why: Good assets may be sold to cure an LTV breach caused by bad ones.
requests.pass: Pledged assets identified; single-asset default does not force sale of unrelated assets without process.

requests.request: Recourse terms: whether the facility has recourse to LP uncalled commitments (hybrid) and on what triggers.
requests.why: Hybrid recourse can force capital calls in a downturn.
requests.pass: Recourse to commitments disclosed to LPs and LPAC-consented.

requests.request: All-in cost: spread, PIK toggle, upfront and commitment fees, compared with the IRR uplift and with selling an asset instead.
requests.why: Facility cost can exceed its benefit; PIK compounds on weak assets.
requests.pass: Cash-pay; all-in cost below the asset-sale alternative.
requests.fail: PIK interest; no comparison with an asset sale.

requests.request: LPA protections for LPs: cap on fund-level leverage, LP or LPAC consent for NAV facilities, no carry on NAV-funded distributions, disclosure of recallability.
requests.why: NAV-funded distributions can pay carry before LPs are whole and can be recalled.
requests.pass: All four protections present.
requests.fail: Carry payable on borrowed distributions or recall terms undisclosed.

requests.request: Subscription-line LPA terms: size and duration caps and LP opt-out.
requests.why: ILPA Principles 3.0 call for reasonable size and duration and an opt-out at the outset.
requests.pass: Caps at or below 25% of commitments and 180 days; opt-out offered.

requests.request: Maturity, extension and renewal terms, and maturities of every other facility in the stack.
requests.why: Haircut and non-renewal spiral as asset prices fall.
requests.pass: Staggered maturities; extension not solely at lender discretion during stress.

requests.request: Pledge structure: holding-company equity pledge description and its position behind portfolio-company lenders.
requests.why: NAV lenders sit behind every portfolio company's own lenders.
requests.pass: Structure and look-through priority disclosed.

requests.request: GP-financing restrictions: LPA and side-letter limits on pledging GP interests or carry, change-of-control and key-person effects, and LP disclosure.
requests.why: GP financing is not covered in the bible; by analogy, LPs need to know when GP economics are leveraged.
requests.pass: Pledge permitted and disclosed to LPs; key-person and change-of-control effects understood.

requests.request: Fund valuation policy and the last two years of marks versus exit prices.
requests.why: Private marks lag public markets by at least four quarters.
requests.pass: Exits at or above prior marks on average.

requests.request: Portfolio-company financial statements and each company's own debt, with look-through leverage.
requests.format: Latest financials and debt schedules per company.
requests.why: Structural subordination: each portfolio company's senior debt sits ahead of the NAV lender.
requests.pass: Look-through leverage computed; no company in default.

requests.request: LTV stress at 25%, 30% and 40% NAV haircuts, identifying when sweep and cure triggers hit.
requests.why: Stale marks and falling values breach LTV late.
requests.pass: No default at a 25% to 40% haircut; sweep triggers early.
requests.fail: Default or forced sale at a 25% haircut.

requests.request: Joint stress: 20% to 30% collateral price fall plus a haircut increase and facility non-renewal, showing which assets are sold first and whether forced sales breach covenants elsewhere.
requests.why: Liquidity can vanish across assets at once; bank-financed booms are the dangerous ones.
requests.pass: Fund survives without forced sales breaching other covenants.

requests.request: Stressed advance-rate analysis: facility sized at crisis-level haircuts.
requests.why: Repo haircuts went from about 0% (early 2007) to nearly 50% (late 2008); Ellington margins from about 10% to above 40%.
requests.pass: Facility serviceable at crisis haircuts.
requests.fail: Facility only works at current advance rates.

requests.request: Complete amendment, waiver and consent history since origination.
requests.why: The amendment trail is the real credit history.
requests.pass: Full history; no pattern of covenant resets.

requests.request: Disclosure sent to LPs about the facility, including ILPA Reporting and Performance Templates.
requests.why: ILPA calls for standardized disclosure to all LPs.
requests.pass: All LPs informed with standardized disclosure.

requests.request: DPI and IRR without the subscription line and without NAV-loan-funded distributions (synthetic DPI).
requests.format: ILPA Performance Template plus synthetic DPI schedule.
requests.why: THE ONE CHECK: without these figures the fund's real liquidity and return are unknown.
requests.pass: Figures produced; differences explained.
requests.fail: GP cannot or will not produce them.
requests.verify: Recompute from cash flows and drawdowns.

requests.request: Confirmation of whether any carry has been or will be paid on NAV-funded distributions.
requests.why: Carry on borrowed distributions pays the GP before LPs are whole.
requests.pass: No carry on NAV-funded distributions.

requests.request: Analysis of whether the facility extends the fund's life or fee stream, with term-extension consents and fee step-downs.
requests.why: Fees run longer on a fund that should be winding down.
requests.pass: Facility maturity within fund term; no fee extension.
requests.fail: Facility requires term extension with full fees.

requests.request: Defensive-use schedule: portfolio companies receiving proceeds, terms, and PIK share.
requests.why: Defensive PIK loans compound leverage on the weakest assets.
requests.pass: Defensive use limited and cash-pay.
requests.fail: PIK rescue loans to struggling companies.

requests.request: Quarterly subscription-line disclosures: size, balance, IRR with and without, uncalled-capital estimate, sub-line interest as a separate expense line.
requests.why: Sub-line-inflated IRR.
requests.pass: Disclosed quarterly.

requests.request: LP commitment schedule and borrowing-base certificate for the subscription line, verified by the administrator.
requests.why: Sub-line collateral is LPs' uncalled commitments.
requests.pass: Borrowing base ties to administrator records; ineligible LPs excluded.

requests.request: Capital-call history and any LP default or late funding.
requests.why: Sub-line repayment depends on LPs funding calls.
requests.pass: No LP defaults.

requests.request: Tax and accounting treatment of recallable NAV-funded distributions for LPs.
requests.why: Recall creates tax and accounting problems for LPs.
requests.pass: Treatment documented.

requests.request: Management-company fee and expense model and existing GP-level debt.
requests.why: GP financing not covered in the bible; GP leverage can affect retention and alignment.
requests.pass: Fees cover expenses and debt service.

requests.request: Independent valuation of the collateral portfolio.
requests.format: Valuation report from an agent engaged by the lender.
requests.why: Stale GP marks hide LTV breaches.
requests.pass: Independent NAV within 10% of GP NAV, or LTV recomputed on independent NAV.

requests.request: Review of the rating-agency methodology applied (KBRA haircut 40% to 60% by asset type; Fitch rates to most conservative permitted terms).
requests.why: Rating stress is the outside view of advance rates.
requests.pass: Facility passes agency stress.

requests.request: Counsel memo on LPA borrowing authority, LPAC consent, recall mechanics and tax.
requests.why: Authority and recall disputes.
requests.pass: No authority gaps.

requests.request: Direct confirmation from the fund administrator of borrowing-base inputs, NAV and capital-call records.
requests.why: Borrowing-base certificates prepared by the GP alone.
requests.pass: Administrator confirms all inputs.

requests.request: Executed facility agreement and fee letter conforming to the agreed term sheet.
requests.why: Late changes.
requests.pass: Only agreed changes.

requests.request: Perfected pledge: holding-company equity pledges, account control agreements and filings.
requests.why: Unperfected security.
requests.pass: All pledges perfected.

requests.request: Executed LPAC consent and evidence of notice to all LPs.
requests.why: Facilities without LPAC consent.
requests.pass: Consent and notices in hand.

requests.request: Closing borrowing-base or LTV certificate.
requests.why: Day-one breach.
requests.pass: Within limits.

requests.request: Periodic borrowing-base and LTV compliance certificates.
requests.why: Late discovery of breaches.
requests.pass: On time and compliant.

requests.request: Quarterly portfolio valuations and independent valuations on lender demand.
requests.why: Stale marks.
requests.pass: Delivered; independent within tolerance.

requests.request: Event notices: asset sales, impairments, portfolio-company defaults.
requests.why: Event-driven LTV tests.
requests.pass: Timely notices.

requests.request: Cash-sweep application report.
requests.why: Sweeps not applied.
requests.pass: Sweep applied per terms.

requests.request: Quarterly facility disclosure to LPs: balances, use of proceeds, IRR and DPI with and without facilities.
requests.why: Undisclosed leverage.
requests.pass: Delivered quarterly.

requests.request: Notice of every amendment, waiver and consent.
requests.why: Amendment trail is the credit history.
requests.pass: Copies within 10 business days.

requests.request: Annual audited financial statements of the fund (and GP entity for GP financing).
requests.why: Valuation drift.
requests.pass: Unqualified and on time.

requests.request: Rating-surveillance reports for rated facilities.
requests.why: Rating migration.
requests.pass: Affirmed.

requests.request: Quarterly subscription-line balance and days outstanding.
requests.why: Sub lines outstanding beyond 180 days.
requests.pass: Within 180 days and 25% of commitments, or disclosed.

kill_tests.test: GP cannot or will not produce DPI and IRR without the sub line and without NAV-loan-funded distributions.
LPA does not permit the facility, or no LPAC consent obtained.
Carry paid or payable on NAV-funded distributions and the GP will not remove it.
LTV tested on GP marks only with no lender independent-valuation right.
Amendment, waiver and consent history refused.
Facility defaults or forces sales at a 25% NAV haircut.

red_flags.flag: NAV facility put in place without LPAC consent.
Use of proceeds is 'distributions' in a fund raising its next vintage.
LTV tested on GP marks only; no independent-valuation right.
Sub line above 25% of commitments or outstanding beyond 180 days without disclosure.
No LP opt-out on the sub line; no with/without reporting.
Multiple layers (sub line plus NAV plus asset-level facilities) with no single map.
Defensive rescue loans to weak portfolio companies.
Facility maturity requires a fund term extension with continued fees.
GP-level debt serviceable only from projected carry.

metrics.acceptable: About $100B (2024) to $600B forecast by 2030 (FFA via ILPA) vs about $100B (2023) to $700B lender forecast (HLS Forum); do not average
About 10% to 30%; maximums around 40% as downside buffers
KBRA haircuts fund value 40% to 60% by asset type
Reportedly rates to the most conservative terms permitted in the facility

metrics.metric: KBRA surveillance, PE and secondary NAV loans 2020-1H 2026
metrics.acceptable: 95% of 279 actions were affirmations (stress not yet tested at scale)
About $8B (2013) to about $95B (end-2024); about 14% of bank lending to nonbanks, up from about 1%
Ellington margins about 10% to above 40% in months
At least four quarters to converge after a shock

third_party_reports.provider: Independent valuation agent (lender right to third-party valuations)
third_party_reports.required_when: Always for NAV and hybrid facilities
Rated facilities and rated feeder notes

third_party_reports.report: Legal memo on borrowing authority, LPAC consent, recall mechanics and tax

hard_questions.question: What is DPI without the NAV loan? IRR without the sub line?
hard_questions.good_answer: Both figures produced immediately from administrator cash flows.

hard_questions.question: What happens at a 30% NAV decline: who cures, and can you recall distributions?
hard_questions.good_answer: A modelled cure waterfall with sweep, no forced sale of good assets, and disclosed recall terms.

hard_questions.question: What does the facility cost all-in against the IRR gain? Why not sell an asset instead?
hard_questions.good_answer: A comparison showing the facility is cheaper than a sale at current secondary pricing.

hard_questions.question: Which assets are pledged, and does one default trigger the whole facility?
hard_questions.good_answer: A pledge schedule with ring-fenced defaults.

hard_questions.question: Who values the collateral for the LTV test?
hard_questions.good_answer: An independent valuation agent with lender appointment rights.

hard_questions.question: Did the LPAC consent, and what were LPs told?
hard_questions.good_answer: Written LPAC consent and standardized ILPA disclosure to all LPs.

hard_questions.question: Is any carry being paid on borrowed distributions?
Show every amendment and waiver since origination.

failure_cases.what_happened: Fund looks liquid and raises next fund on borrowed distributions.
failure_cases.check: Recompute DPI excluding NAV-funded distributions; ILPA Performance Template.

failure_cases.case: Recall of distributions in a downturn (generic)
failure_cases.what_happened: LPs must return cash when they least have it.
failure_cases.check: Read the recall clause and LTV cure waterfall; model a 30% NAV drawdown.

failure_cases.what_happened: Good assets sold to cure an LTV breach caused by bad ones.
failure_cases.check: Map pledged assets; single-asset default triggers.

failure_cases.what_happened: GP paid before LPs are whole.
failure_cases.check: LPA: no carry on NAV-funded distributions.

failure_cases.case: Defensive PIK loans to rescue weak companies (generic)
failure_cases.what_happened: Leverage compounds on the weakest assets.
Fees run longer on a fund that should be winding down.
IRR rises with no change in multiple.
Lender cuts advance rate as asset prices fall; repo haircuts went from about 0% to nearly 50%.
failure_cases.check: Stress haircuts to crisis levels; staggered maturities.
